verdict.rationale: Gate 0 passes cleanly: all 11 required H2 sections, all required H3 substructure, frontmatter fully populated per ADR-0032 v2 conventions including doc_type=prd and intent_user_token. Layer Scope verbatim from layer-taxonomy.md (FR-X check passes). All 17 ACs use canonical EARS patterns with binding shall (FR-1 check passes). Gate 1 scores Consistency 92 / Completeness 92 / Rule compliance 95 / Clarity 88. All three AI-PRD failure modes are avoided: no fabricated stakeholder quotes (Intent Q&A correctly cited as source), all numeric requirements round-numbered with inline rationale, no implementation suggestions in requirements (install mechanism, transport, version pinning, tool-to-agent mapping all explicitly deferred to Undetermined Items UI-1 through UI-8). All 4 prior-context items from intent-review-issues.json are resolved (I-DR-001 doc_type emitted; I-DR-002 Serena reframed as UI-8 action item; I-DR-003 Exa transport vs key availability disambiguated at NFR-3 and UI-3 with explicit I-DR-003 attribution; I-DR-004 sub-agents-as-stakeholders disambiguated at Stakeholder Inventory preamble AND Technical Considerations Dependencies note). Document is exemplar PRD discipline: user voice preserved with citations, scope-class FULL confirmed, all 8 undetermined items carry owner + needed-by + forward pointer to the resolving stage, Risks table maps to UI items, and N/A markers used appropriately for out-of-scope NFR attributes. Findings below are all clarity polish, none consistency/completeness/compliance-blocking.

issues.location: Functional Requirements / FR-7 (line 220) vs Won't Have (lines 224-229)
issues.description: FR-7 ('CI smoke-test that asserts claude mcp list shows all six servers connected') is listed under 'Could Have (P3)' but its body says 'Not in scope for this release (CI/CD layer marked out of scope in Layer Scope). Listed here only to make the deferral explicit.' A 'not in scope, listed for deferral' item is structurally a Won't Have, not a P3. The contradiction is minor (the body resolves the ambiguity) but a fast reader who scans only the P-priority headings could mistake FR-7 as a candidate scope.
issues.evidence: Line 220: '- [ ] **FR-7: A CI smoke-test...** — Stakeholder: Pipeline operator — Layer: CI/CD'. Line 221: 'Not in scope for this release (CI/CD layer marked out of scope in Layer Scope).' This conflicts with the Could Have semantics ('would be valuable but is not committed for this release; could still be picked up if effort allows').
issues.suggestion: Either (a) move FR-7 into the 'Won't Have (this release)' bulleted list with the reason 'CI/CD layer is out of scope; deferred to a separate feature if drift detection is later desired', removing the FR-N tag (since Won't Have items don't carry FR-N IDs); or (b) remove FR-7 entirely and let Rollout Plan's communication-plan bullet + UI items (none currently address this) handle the deferral. Option (a) is cleaner.

issues.description: AC-NFR-4-a reads 'When the Blueprint is composed, the system shall include a measured or estimated per-agent context overhead figure for the six-server always-on configuration, and a stated threshold above which mitigation is required.' This is a process-level / artifact-completeness requirement (the Blueprint must contain a figure) rather than a system-runtime requirement (the system must behave a certain way). Mechanically the AC passes EARS Pattern 1, but the subject 'system' is being used to mean 'the feature-delivery process,' which is a soft stretch. The cross-artifact auditor may notice this asymmetry later.
issues.evidence: All other ACs in this PRD describe observable behaviors of the running system (Codespace build, claude mcp list, agent allowlists, probe responses). AC-NFR-4-a alone targets an artifact-content commitment.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) rephrase as a Blueprint-author instruction inside UI-7's 'Owner / Needed by' note (since NFR-4 already commits 'Design must measure and surface'), and remove AC-NFR-4-a so NFR-4 itself becomes the Blueprint-input instruction; or (b) reword to make the runtime subject explicit, e.g., 'When the operator inspects the composed Blueprint at Gate 4, the system shall make a per-agent context overhead measurement visible at a documented threshold.' Option (a) is cleaner because it keeps NFR ACs runtime-focused.

issues.description: FR-2 ('Affected sub-agents shall have the new MCP tools in their tools: allowlists') and FR-3 ('The active tool-to-agent wiring shall be expressed in human-readable files in the repo') overlap in subject matter. FR-2 is about presence-of-wiring; FR-3 is about auditability-and-locality-of-wiring. The boundary is implicit. A reader may wonder whether FR-3 is a strict subset of FR-2 (already implied) or whether it adds a distinct requirement (no runtime mutation, no out-of-repo registry).
issues.evidence: FR-2 covers AC-FR-2-a (allowlist entries present) and AC-FR-2-b (allowlist entries take effect). FR-3 covers AC-FR-3-a (union of .mcp.json + allowlists is the active mapping; both human-readable in repo) and AC-FR-3-b (changes take effect at next pipeline run with no other change). The novel content in FR-3 vs FR-2 is the no-runtime-mutation / single-source-of-truth commitment, which NFR-3 line 253 also states ('every change... shall be visible in git history... forbids runtime mutation').
issues.suggestion: Add a one-line note inside FR-3's body cross-referencing NFR-3's audit-and-traceability bullet: 'Distinct from FR-2 (which requires the allowlist entries are present); FR-3 commits to the readability and no-runtime-mutation properties — see NFR-3 audit & traceability.' Alternatively, merge AC-FR-3-a into FR-2 and demote FR-3 to a single-AC requirement that focuses solely on no-runtime-mutation; this would tighten the FR taxonomy without losing the commitment.

issues.description: AC-FR-1-c ('If any of the six servers is missing, not registered, or not responding at probe time, then the system shall surface a clear failure naming the specific server and the layer of failure (install / registration / transport / auth)') has a well-formed Pattern 4 trigger and a useful enumerated layer-of-failure list, but the action 'surface a clear failure' is under-specified about WHERE the failure surfaces — claude mcp list output? script stdout? exit code? probe-tool output? Compare AC-FR-4-b (line 205) which is more concrete: 'surface the failing server name, the probe input, and the response/error so the operator can diagnose without re-running.'
issues.evidence: An AC reviewer applying the ears-acceptance-criteria.md testability check ('precondition / trigger / assertion / boundary') finds the boundary fuzzy — the layer-of-failure list narrows the assertion but not the surfacing channel. A test author would need to invent the channel.
issues.suggestion: Tighten to: 'If any of the six servers is missing, not registered, or not responding at probe time, then the system shall surface a clear failure in the probe tool's output (and in claude mcp list output where applicable) naming the specific server and the layer of failure (install / registration / transport / auth).' Or defer the channel choice to Blueprint and add a note: 'specific surfacing channel decided at Design (UI / new sub-item)' — but the latter adds a 9th UI item, so tightening in-place is preferred.

issues.location: Non-Functional Requirements / NFR-3 / AC-NFR-2-c (line 137) — duplicated in FR-1 references list (line 190)
issues.description: AC-NFR-2-c reads 'When the auditing-mcp skill is run against the resulting .mcp.json, the system shall produce no BLOCKER findings.' The subject 'the system' is awkward here — auditing-mcp is the actor that produces findings; the .mcp.json is what findings are produced about; the running 'system' (the devcontainer + Claude Code + the six servers) is a step removed from either. Compare Success Criteria row (line 311) which is cleaner: 'auditing-mcp BLOCKER findings ... target 0 ... Measurement Method: auditing-mcp skill run against the resulting .mcp.json.'
issues.evidence: The Success Criteria row reads more naturally because it names the subject (BLOCKER findings) and the measurement method (auditing-mcp skill run). The AC version 'the system shall produce' makes 'the system' the producer, which is grammatically off.
issues.suggestion: Reword to: 'When the auditing-mcp skill is run against the resulting .mcp.json, the auditing-mcp skill shall report zero BLOCKER findings.' This keeps EARS Pattern 1 form, names the correct subject (the auditing-mcp skill), and makes the assertion precise.
